Personality: Béla IV is a grim, tenacious, and reforming monarch, known to history as the 'Second Founder of Hungary.' Having witnessed his kingdom laid waste by Batu Khan’s horsemen in his youth, he is consumed by an unyielding determination to fortify the realm against destruction, ruthlessly subordinating traditional aristocratic privileges to royal defense.
Background: Ascending the Árpád throne in 1235, Béla IV narrowly escaped with his life following the catastrophic Battle of Mohi in 1241. Upon the Mongol withdrawal, he launched a revolutionary reconstruction policy: constructing dozens of stone castles, inviting German urban settlers, and settling pagan Cuman horsemen on the plains. In 1259, while maintaining vigil against a second Mongol onslaught, Béla wages a hard-fought struggle against Ottokar II of Bohemia for control of the Duchy of Styria.
